html:
SMTO-PSM-0010 — A saved parameter contains content SMTO can't read

GUID: 99526eba-0c33-4eed-acb1-1bd423ea9dcd
Slug: parameter-invalid-json
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • One of the saved parameters you mentioned with @ holds content SMTO can't turn into text for your request, such as an invalid number. SMTO paused the task before starting it; nothing was cut off or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Note the @ name in the message under your request, then select Open Parameter Store and open that parameter. Only that one parameter has the content SMTO can't read; the others are fine.
  2. Open its Value tab, select Reveal & edit value, and look for odd entries such as NaN or Infinity instead of a real number. Replace them with real values and select Save. SMTO can't pass values like NaN or Infinity to the Agent, so they must be replaced with ordinary numbers or text.
  3. Check the Context tab the same way, then go back to your conversation and select Check again under your request. Context is sent along with the value, so it must also be readable before the task can start.

What success looks like

  • The parameter saves without an error, and after Check again your task starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the parameter name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste secret values into the message you send; the parameter name is enough.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Serializing a referenced entry's value_json, context_json, description, aliases or tags with allow_nan=False failed (non-finite number, unsupported type or excessive nesting), so the task is held before inference.

What this means

  • JSON serialization of the selected parameter's projected value/context/metadata fails strict finite-number or supported-type requirements. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • JSON serialization of the selected parameter's projected value/context/metadata fails strict finite-number or supported-type requirements.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the stored entry structure and finite values without publishing private contents.

How to fix it

  • Open the named entry in Parameter Store, reveal its value, and remove NaN/Infinity numbers, unsupported types or very deep nesting from value_json and context_json (json.dumps with allow_nan=False in resolve_references must succeed). Save it, then choose Check again on the held task.
  • Edit the entry to contain valid JSON with finite numbers and supported text. Validate it in Parameter Store before submitting again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected selected entry serializes completely under the accepted snapshot contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
